quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Get out and flag down the next passing vehicle.
Pull to the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on an interstate or highway shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high speed of traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving, such as struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or needing the radio loud to stay awake. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest with a short nap.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider ahead.
A lane is ending soon. Traffic must move to the left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending soon. Traffic must move to the left.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It warns that one or more lanes ahead will end and traffic needs to merge left.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Stop until they are completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog while crossing, you must stop until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, where should you look?
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left side will be closer to you than those from your right. Check that the entire intersection is clear before moving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are driving the wrong way on a one-way street.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are driving the wrong way on a one-way street.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road, entrance, or exit. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around immediately if you are driving toward this sign.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under ideal conditions. It is safest to match the speed of surrounding traffic, up to the limit. All drivers share the responsibility of driving safely at the right speed.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Drinking coffee, eating, or taking a shower cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: What should you do if you start to feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Try to fight the feeling and keep driving.

questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the nearest rest stop or service area to take a break, nap, or stretch. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. These are not a substitute for real rest and can make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear your seat belt?

options.text: Yes, always wear your seat belt.
Wear the belt loosely behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety features. For the best protection in a crash, always use your lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

questions.question: Your reaction time slows down after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: You should change lanes:

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, you should:
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. However, if a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes driving mistakes and increases your crash risk. When tired, you take longer to make decisions. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can sleep while they drive.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas to slow down gradually. Do not apply the brakes until your vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go ahead if you have the right-of-way.
Go ahead if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians in the intersection. If a pedestrian begins crossing after the signal flashes, wait until they finish crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to turn safely.

questions.question: When should you yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if they wave at you.
Only if they are not texting.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let any vehicles or pedestrians cross. You may proceed carefully if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, coordination, and alertness. They also reduce your ability to concentrate.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your windows before driving. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you start to drive.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look at your blind spot before you move left or right.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Keep extra distance between your car and the car ahead. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black words means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-way road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to let them pass and get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: You want to turn right at the corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. Before you turn, you should:

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians who use guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip) have the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you move. Also adjust your seat, fasten your belt, and secure items in your car. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: What happens if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair your driving. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.
Increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your blood alcohol content. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not help. You must wait for alcohol to leave your system.
